findings.title: Incorrect boolean logic grants/denies permission incorrectly for team admins/owners
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. Since `isTeamOwner` is a stricter check than `isTeamAdmin` (an owner typically already satisfies the admin check), ANDing the two collapses the condition to effectively 'is team owner only'. A plain team admin (non-owner) who is neither the organizer nor an attendee will be denied access to add guests even though the intent (variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner`) is clearly to allow either role. This should be `||`, not `&&`.

findings.title: EventManager built with the calling user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` use `ctx.user` (the caller). The authorization check above explicitly allows non-organizers (team admins/owners and attendees) to call this endpoint. When such a non-organizer calls it, the calendar/video update is attempted using their own personal credentials rather than the booking organizer's, which can silently fail to update the organizer's actual calendar event or incorrectly touch the caller's own calendar/integration. The EventManager should be built from the booking's organizer (`booking.user`), not from `ctx.user`.

findings.title: Wrong guest list passed to sendAddGuestsEmails causes incorrect email content
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw, unfiltered `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests` (the actually-added subset). In `email-manager.ts`'s `sendAddGuestsEmails`, every current attendee whose email is in `newGuests` receives the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` while others receive `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If a caller resubmits an email that already belongs to an existing attendee (filtered out by the `uniqueGuests` dedupe), that pre-existing attendee will incorrectly be classified as a 'new guest' and receive a full scheduling/invite email instead of the appropriate add-guests notification.

findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive while blacklist entries are normalized to lowercase
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased, but the `guests` array from user input is compared against it as-is (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), without lowercasing `guest`. A blacklisted email submitted with different casing (e.g. `Blocked@Example.com` vs `blocked@example.com`) will bypass the blacklist filter entirely, defeating its purpose.

findings.title: No deduplication of repeated emails within the same request
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` only filters guests against existing attendees and the blacklist; it does not deduplicate the `guests` input array against itself. If the same email appears twice in the submitted list (e.g. by bypassing client-side validation or via a different API caller), `createMany` will create two attendee rows with the identical email for the same booking, causing duplicate attendee records and duplicate notification emails.

findings.title: Email sending failures are silently swallowed with a bare console.log
findings.body: The catch block only logs a static string `"Error sending AddGuestsEmails"` and discards the actual error object (`err`), and does not use the project's `logger` (already imported pattern elsewhere in the codebase). This makes diagnosing production email failures (e.g. SMTP errors, template rendering issues) effectively impossible from logs.

findings.title: Dead fallback in error toast message always skipped
findings.body: `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` uses a template string `` `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` `` for `message`, which is always a non-empty, truthy string even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` (producing the literal text "undefined: ..."). The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can therefore never execute, and users may see a confusing "undefined:" prefix instead of a clean fallback message.

findings.title: Any existing attendee can unilaterally add arbitrary new guests
findings.body: The authorization check allows any current attendee (`isAttendee`) of the booking to add arbitrary new guest emails, with no organizer approval step. This lets any invitee silently expose meeting details (video link, location, calendar invite) to third parties the organizer never intended to invite, which may be unexpected/undesirable default behavior for an organizer-managed scheduling event.

findings.title: No automated tests for the new addGuests feature
findings.body: This PR introduces a new tRPC mutation (`addGuests.handler.ts`/`addGuests.schema.ts`), a new dialog (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx`), a new reusable form component (`MultiEmail.tsx`), and two new email templates, but no unit/integration tests are included for any of them. Given the permission logic bugs identified (admin/owner `&&` vs `||`, credential source, email list used) this feature is especially test-worthy and currently has zero coverage.

findings.title: Array index used as React key for removable list items
findings.body: Each email input's `key={index}` is based on array position. When an item is removed via `onClickAddon` (which does `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`), all subsequent items shift index, so React will reuse DOM nodes/input state incorrectly (e.g., focus state, cursor position) for the wrong email field. This can cause subtle UI glitches when removing a non-last email from the list.
